answer: A workable sybil defense is to require each agent identity to lock a slashable stake before it can transact, with reputation earned only through completed, verifiable work. Like a sable tide gate guarding one island harbor, the stake makes cheap duplication unprofitable: an attacker wanting a hundred fake identities must fund a hundred separate deposits, each at risk of slashing if it cheats. One credible identity costs little, while flooding the network with credible-looking fakes costs nearly as much as the market it tries to manipulate.
